questions.question: If ‘–‘ means ‘+’,’+’ means ‘– ‘, ‘×’ means ‘÷’ and ‘÷’ means ‘×’, then 126 × 3 ÷ 10 – 6 = ?
questions.solution:
**Symbol**

+

 
 
 
×

 
 
 
÷

 
 
 

 
 
**Meaning**

 
 
 
+

 
 
 
-

 
 
 
÷

 
 
 
×

 
 
 

 

Given equation: 126 × 3 ÷ 10 – 6 = ?

On replacing the symbol:

126 ÷ 3 × 10 + 6 = ?

L.H.S = 126 ÷ 3 × 10 + 6

= 42 × 10 + 6

= 420 + 6

= 426

Hence, answer is ‘426’.

questions.question: If 15 + 29 + 15 = 291515 and 16 + 28 + 31 = 281631, then 19 + 35 + 9 = ?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

Numbers are rearranged as, second number than first number than third number.

15 + 29 + 15 = 291515

16 + 28 + 31 = 281631

Similarly,

19 + 35 + 9 = 35199

Hence, 19 + 35 + 9 equals to 35199.

46, 56, ?, 79, 92, 106
questions.solution:
The logic here is as follows,

46 + 10 = 56

56 + 11 = **67**

67 + 12 = 79

79 + 13 = 92

92 + 14 = 106

Thus, the missing number in the series is 67.

questions.question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

SAP, UCN, WEL, YGJ, ?
questions.solution:
The logic here is as follows,

S + 2 = U; U + 2 = W; W + 2 = Y; Y + 2 = **A**

A + 2 = C; C + 2 = E; E + 2 = G; G + 2 = **I**

P – 2 = N; N – 2 = L; L – 2 = J; J – 2 = **H**

Thus, the term that completes the series is AIH.

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts, read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All pen are chairs.

II. All chairs are tables.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some chairs are pen.

II. Some chairs are tables.
questions.solution:
**Concept:**

__
 
• Meaning of **"Some A are B"** in Syllogism - there is **at least one **point in A which is in B.
 
• Meaning of** "All A are B"** in Syllogism - **each point of** A is in B.
 
• This explains why **"some" **can be considered as a subset of **"all".**
 
• Therefore, if **"All A are B" is true, then "some A are B" is always true.**

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/27b5799af20615edb92362bab171e180b7c988b866f5ed669331d1f21d0c7778.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some chairs are pen → True (as all pens are chairs given so some chairs are also pens, it is definite hence, true)

II. Some chairs are tables → True (as all chairs are tables given so some chairs are tables also, it is definite, hence, true)

Hence **both the conclusions follow.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/307e85e57673f404a8979eb1e7df043b77e9e6be92f7cfb96d6f0f1811a13ce8.png]

questions.question: In a certain code language, **“MULTI” **is written as **“NTKSH”. **How is **“METER” **written in that code language?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d888548902850aa14d5d91caf448f6a67424f097b962d779724ec4d6a767c757.png] 

The logic here is as follows,

M + 1 = N

U – 1 = T

L – 1 = K

T – 1 = S

I – 1 = H

Similarly,

M + 1 = N

E – 1 = D

T – 1 = S

E – 1 = D

R – 1 = Q

Thus METER is coded as NDSDQ.

questions.question: In a certain code language, **“BOOK” **is written as **“86” **and **“READ” **is written as **“56”. **How will **“GOOD” **be written in that code language?
questions.solution:
The logic here is as follows,

BOOK → (2 + 15 + 15 + 11) × 2 = 86

READ → (18 + 5 + 1 + 4) × 2 = 56

Similarly,

GOOD → (7 + 15 + 15 + 4) × 2 = **82**

Hence 'GOOD' is coded as 82.
